This is acceptable because the local raymarching network handles empty space (no image contribution), while missing surfaces clearly reduces image quality [S1].

The claim states that filtering is acceptable because the local raymarching network handles empty space (no image contribution) and missing surfaces reduce image quality. Source [S1] explicitly supports this reasoning in the notes and passages. The notes state: 'Filtering increases false positives (likelihood for sampling regions that do not need samples) but decreases false negatives. This is acceptable because the local raymarching network handles empty space (no image contribution) and missing surfaces clearly reduces image quality.' The passages further elaborate: 'Translating a higher false positive rate to raymarching, we increase the likelihood for sampling regions that do not need any samples... A missed surface on the other hand would clearly reduce image quality.' Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
